transcript:
[Doctor]: Hi Maria, how are you doing today?

[Patient]: Hi, doctor. Not great, to be honest. I've been feeling really down.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

[Patient]: For the past two months, I've been feeling really sad all the time. I used to love painting, but now I don't even want to pick up a brush. I'm just so tired every day.

[Doctor]: Hmm, okay. So you've been feeling persistently sad and lost interest in activities you used to enjoy. What about your energy levels?

[Patient]: They're really low. I feel exhausted all the time, even if I haven't done much.

[Doctor]: I see. Have you noticed any changes in your appetite?

[Patient]: Yes, I've been eating a lot of fast food and sugary snacks lately. I just don't have the energy to cook.

[Doctor]: That makes sense. How about your sleep? Are you having trouble sleeping?

[Patient]: Yes, I have a lot of trouble falling asleep and staying asleep. When I do sleep, I wake up feeling just as tired as before.

[Doctor]: Alright, so difficulty falling and staying asleep, and feeling unrested. How has all this been affecting your job and social life?

[Patient]: It's been really hard. I work part-time in retail, and I can barely keep up with my shifts. I don't hang out with my friends much anymore either.

[Doctor]: I understand. Now, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself?

[Patient]: No, I haven't. But sometimes I feel hopeless, like things will never get better.

[Doctor]: That's very important to note. Do you smoke or use any substances?

[Patient]: I used to smoke but quit five years ago. I drink about 3-4 glasses of wine a week, more on weekends. I occasionally use marijuana.

[Doctor]: Okay, thanks for sharing that. Let's move on to a quick physical exam. I'll be calling out some of my findings as we go along, and I'll explain what they mean afterward, alright?

[Patient]: Sure.

[Doctor]: Your blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg and your heart rate is 75 bpm. Your skin looks normal with no abnormalities. Your cardiovascular and respiratory exams are normal. Your abdomen is soft and non-tender, and your extremities have normal reflexes with no edema. Overall, you appear tired and have poor eye contact, which fits with what you've described. 

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: We're still waiting on your Complete Blood Count and Thyroid Function Test results, which will help rule out any other potential issues like hypothyroidism.

[Patient]: Got it.

[Doctor]: Based on everything we've discussed and your physical exam, it sounds like you're experiencing a severe episode of Major Depressive Disorder. This has significantly impacted your daily functioning and quality of life.

[Patient]: Yeah, it really has.

[Doctor]: For your treatment, I would like to start you on Sertraline 50 mg, taken orally once daily. This medication can help improve your mood and energy levels.

[Patient]: I'm a bit skeptical about medications. Will it really help?

[Doctor]: It's understandable to feel that way. While it may take a few weeks for the medication to take full effect, many people do find it helpful. Along with the medication, I'm going to refer you to a psychologist for cognitive-behavioral therapy, which can also be very effective.

[Patient]: Okay, I can try that.

[Doctor]: Great. Let's also set up a follow-up visit in four weeks to see how you're responding to the medication.

[Patient]: Alright.

[Doctor]: In the meantime, I encourage you to try some regular physical activity, even a short walk can help improve your mood and energy. Also, try to make healthier dietary choices and avoid fast food and sugary snacks.

[Patient]: I'll try.

[Doctor]: We'll also discuss some sleep hygiene techniques to help improve your sleep quality. Simple changes like keeping a regular sleep schedule and creating a restful environment can make a big difference.

[Patient]: That sounds good.

[Doctor]: I'll provide you with some educational materials on the nature of depression and what to expect with your treatment. I'll also give you information on local mental health services and support resources.

[Patient]: Thank you, I appreciate that.

[Doctor]: We'll monitor for any adverse effects of the medication and adjust the treatment plan if necessary. It's really important to stay on the prescribed treatment and keep your follow-up appointments.

[Patient]: I understand.

[Doctor]: Do you have any questions or concerns right now?

[Patient]: No, I think you covered everything.

[Doctor]: Excellent. Remember, if you have any concerns or questions before our next appointment, feel free to call the office or message me through the patient portal.

[Patient]: Thank you, doctor. I will.

[Doctor]: You're welcome, Maria. We'll see you in four weeks. Take care.

[Patient]: Thanks, doctor. Bye.

[Doctor]: Bye, Maria.
